meta.title: The Barrier You Paid For
meta.subtitle: A structural change cannot start until every tracked job everywhere in the world has finished — and the bill arrives twice

views.label: Why it has to stop
views.note: Moving an entity invalidates raw pointers into chunks. Any job still holding one would be reading freed memory.

views.label: It is not selective
views.note: Not the jobs that touch this archetype. Every fence of every type, combined into one handle, then waited on.

views.label: The bill you are not shown
views.note: The stall is the visible cost. The dropped chunk-list caches are billed to whichever system iterates next.

views.label: Paying once instead of often
views.note: Recording defers the change to a known system, so many small barriers collapse into one you can see in the profiler.

states.label: Record it instead
states.sublabel: played back at a known system

cards.title: What the barrier actually is
items: Every structural change calls the same guard first · EntityDataAccess.cs:406
Which completes all jobs and invalidates arrays · EntityDataAccess.cs:415
That combines the fences of every registered type into one handle · ComponentDependencyManager.cs:147
Waits on it, then forgets every fence it was tracking · ComponentDependencyManager.cs:148

cards.title: How to see one in the profiler
items: The wait is wrapped in a marker literally named CompleteAllJobs · ComponentDependencyManager.cs:120
It is skipped entirely when no fences are registered · ComponentDependencyManager.cs:143
So a frame with no scheduled jobs pays nothing for its structural changes
And a frame with a deep job graph pays for the deepest chain in it

cards.title: The bill nobody shows you
items: After the change, new archetypes are pushed to every query · EntityDataAccess.cs:489
Then every changed archetype drops its queries' chunk caches · EntityDataAccess.cs:492
The walk follows a linked list of archetypes touched this batch · EntityComponentStore.cs:2682
Those caches are rebuilt lazily, so the cost lands on the next system to iterate

cards.title: The three honest levers
items: Record into a command buffer so many barriers become one · EntityCommandBufferSystem.cs:180
Use enableable components so a boolean never moves an entity between chunks
Operate on a whole query at once rather than one entity at a time
There is also an attribute that forces a barrier every update, if you truly need one · AlwaysSynchronizeSystemAttribute.cs:11
